tasks.title: Operation select: AND or OR
tasks.statement: The simplest ALU performs two operations on bits A and B. Input Op selects which one: Op = 0 gives Y = A AND B, Op = 1 gives Y = A OR B. Both operations are always computed, but only the selected one reaches the output.
tasks.hint: Two compute units, A AND B and A OR B, and a multiplexer at the output: Y = ¬Op·(A·B) OR Op·(A+B). You built the multiplexer in the section on signal selection.

tasks.title: Four logic operations
tasks.statement: Add more operations. Code Op1 Op0 selects: 00 is A AND B, 01 is A OR B, 10 is A XOR B, 11 is NOT A (B is ignored). Output Y is the result of the selected operation.
tasks.hint: Four compute units (AND, OR, XOR, NOT A) and a 4→1 multiplexer driven by Op1 Op0: a tree of three 2→1 multiplexers, as in the section on signal selection. If XOR is locked, build it from AND, OR and NOT.

tasks.title: Result flags
tasks.statement: An ALU does not just produce a number: it also reports “flags” about it. From the two-bit result R1 R0, produce three: Z, the result is zero; N, the result is negative (the top bit in two's complement is the sign); Pe, the number of ones in the result is even.
tasks.hint: Z is a single NOR gate: zero when both bits are zero. N is just a wire from R1. Pe is bit equality (XNOR): the number of ones is even when the bits are the same.

tasks.title: Increment and decrement
tasks.statement: Two special ALU actions: “+1” and “−1”. The two-bit value A1 A0 changes by one in either direction, wrapping around: with Dec = 0 the result is A + 1 (11 → 00), with Dec = 1 it is A − 1 (00 → 11). Output R1 R0.
tasks.hint: The low bit always flips: R0 = ¬A0. The high bit: for +1 it flips if A0 = 1 (R1 = A1⊕A0); for −1 it flips if A0 = 0 (R1 = A1⊕¬A0 = A1⊕A0⊕1). Both cases combine into R1 = A1⊕A0⊕Dec.

tasks.title: Overflow flag
tasks.statement: Two-bit signed numbers (in two's complement) range from −2 to 1: 00 = 0, 01 = 1, 10 = −2, 11 = −1. Add A and B and output V = 1 if the true result does NOT fit in this range (for example, 01 + 01 = 2 is an overflow).
tasks.hint: Overflow happens only when the operands have the same sign (A1 = B1) and the sum's sign S1 is different. S1 needs the carry from the low bit, c = A0·B0: S1 = A1⊕B1⊕c. Then V = (A1 ⊙ B1) · (A1 ⊕ S1).

tasks.title: Shifter
tasks.statement: A shift is also an ALU operation: multiplication or division by two. The two-bit value A1 A0 is shifted left (Dir = 0: R = A0 0) or right (Dir = 1: R = 0 A1). The bit that “falls off” goes to output Co.
tasks.hint: Each output is a choice by Dir. R1 = ¬Dir·A0 (on a right shift the top bit is zero); R0 = Dir·A1; Co = ¬Dir·A1 OR Dir·A0. One inverter for Dir.

tasks.title: ALU bit slice
tasks.statement: Build one bit slice of an ALU. Inputs: A, B, carry Cin and operation code Op1 Op0: 00 is addition (A + B + Cin), 01 is subtraction (A + ¬B + Cin), 10 is A AND B, 11 is A OR B. Outputs: result bit R and carry Co (for logic operations Co = 0).
tasks.hint: Three blocks. Arithmetic: bx = B⊕Op0 (inverts B for subtraction), then a full adder on A, bx, Cin. Logic: an AND / OR multiplexer driven by Op0. Final: a multiplexer driven by Op1, arithmetic (Op1 = 0) or logic (Op1 = 1). Take the carry Co only when Op1 = 0.

tasks.title: Arithmetic: addition and subtraction
tasks.statement: The arithmetic block of a two-bit ALU. Mode M = 0 is A + B, M = 1 is A − B (that is, A + ¬B + 1). Outputs: R1 R0 is the result, Co is the carry out of the top bit (in subtraction Co = 1 means “no borrow”, i.e. A ≥ B).
tasks.hint: A controlled inverter on B: bm = B⊕M for each bit. Then the two-bit adder from the previous section, but the carry into the low bit equals M: R0 = A0⊕bm0⊕M, c0 = A0·bm0 OR (A0⊕bm0)·M, then the high bit as usual.

tasks.title: Two-bit logic
tasks.statement: The logic block of a two-bit ALU. Input Op selects the operation on each pair of bits: Op = 0 is bitwise AND, Op = 1 is bitwise OR. Output R1 R0.
tasks.hint: Two identical “bit slices” sharing Op: each computes AND and OR, and a multiplexer driven by Op picks one of them. You need only one inverter for Op, shared by both bits.

tasks.title: Two-bit ALU
tasks.statement: The finale: combine arithmetic and logic. Code Op1 Op0 selects the operation on A1 A0 and B1 B0: 00 is A + B, 01 is A − B, 10 is A AND B, 11 is A OR B. Output R1 R0 is the result (modulo 4).
tasks.hint: Do not rebuild everything: these are the same two blocks. Arithmetic: M = Op0, with the result R1 R0 from the previous exercise (Co is not needed). Logic: Op = Op0. Then at each output a multiplexer driven by Op1: arithmetic when Op1 = 0, logic when Op1 = 1. About thirty gates in all, so build it in parts.

tasks.title: Comparison via subtraction
tasks.statement: How does a processor compare numbers? It subtracts and looks at the result! For two-bit unsigned A and B, produce Lt (A < B), Eq (A = B), Gt (A > B) using the subtraction A − B = A + ¬B + 1.
tasks.hint: Subtractor: nb = ¬B. The low bit with carry-in 1 simplifies: R0 = A0⊙nb0, c0 = A0 OR nb0. The high bit: x = A1⊕nb1, R1 = x⊕c0, Co = A1·nb1 + x·c0. Then: Eq = ¬(R1+R0) (the difference is zero), Lt = ¬Co (there was a borrow), Gt = Co·¬Eq.

tasks.title: Branch condition
tasks.statement: Flags are needed to decide whether the program continues or jumps. From flags Z (zero), N (sign), V (overflow) and condition code C1 C0, produce T, “condition met”: 00 is “equal” (Z), 01 is “not equal” (¬Z), 10 is “less” (N⊕V), 11 is “less or equal” (Z OR N⊕V).
tasks.hint: First compute all four conditions: Z, ¬Z, lt = N⊕V and le = Z OR lt. Then a 4→1 multiplexer driven by C1 C0 selects one: a tree of three 2→1 multiplexers.
